title: Localization of a normalized global projection package
statement: Fix f:X to Y, ring sheaves RY,RX and an identification f-inverse RY isomorphic to RX. For every Global datum g of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction-data] and every object V of Y-pro-etale, there is a Local datum l at V satisfying ProjectionCompatible. This conclusion constructs one localized square from the supplied global package; it does not construct that global package or assert local detection of derived isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), 0FN5 (lemma-localize-cartesian-square-modules), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); slice-topos restriction of the counit map 0B56.

proof.text: Localize the site morphism at V and its base change. Evaluate the original ring map at underlying objects. Both direct-image routes have identical sections and scalar actions, giving the identity comparison. Its adjunction mate is the module pullback comparison. Restriction is exact.

Restriction preserves K-injectives because its extension-by-zero left adjoint is exact. Derive the identity section square using K-injective representatives, obtaining the prescribed right-derived normalization. Take its inverse adjunction mate. The counit equation follows from the adjunction bijection; the representative formula identifies the mate with the ordinary localized square.

Construct tensor models on both localized sites and derive the ordinary tensor pullback and restriction comparisons. The ordinary localization square sends each local pure tensor to the same pure tensor along either route. Totalization respects both integer shifts, including the second-variable Koszul sign, and full faithfulness descends all these equations.

Apply tensor coherence to this ordinary localized square. Transpose the counit-tensor composite under the derived adjunction. Its counit-mate equation and tensor coherence identify the two resulting paths. Under the explicit source and target composites this is precisely ProjectionCompatible. The argument works for any given global package because all its comparisons are normalized on the same representatives.

theorem localModel_exists {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (R_Y : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (R_X : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R_Y ≅ R_X)
    (g : Global f R_Y R_X c) (V : Y.ProEt) :
    ∃ l : Local f R_Y R_X c g V, l.ProjectionCompatible
